**Orange signs on as first French merchant to offer Wero for bill payments**

*A commercial turning point for EPI's pan-European payment scheme, as the move from peer-to-peer transfers into recurring merchant billing reaches its first named retailer in France.*

Orange, the French telecoms group, has agreed to accept Wero for subscription bill payments – the first merchant in France to sign up for the capability. The European Payments Initiative (EPI) developed Wero initially for person-to-person transfers, and extending it to recurring merchant billing represents the scheme's clearest step yet toward becoming a viable alternative to card networks at the point of sale. Wero's subscription payment features are not yet live; EPI has indicated they are planned for 2027, making Orange's commitment a statement of intent rather than an operational launch.

France is EPI's home market and second-largest by user base after Germany. ING expanded Wero in June to include online retail payments for existing users who had activated peer-to-peer functionality since August 2025. BoursoBank announced a partnership agreement the same month to integrate Wero by the end of 2026, and Credit Agricole completed France's first production agentic payment via the scheme. Orange's agreement signals that the bill-payment use case – critical for proving Wero can handle commercial volume – is building institutional support even before recurring payments go live.

Recurring billing is a natural entry point for account-to-account schemes competing with card-on-file, because the payment relationship is already established and consumer friction is lower than at checkout. Broader e-commerce adoption remains uncertain, but a household brand like Orange committing to the option normalises the scheme for French consumers in a way that peer-to-peer alone could not.

*Sources: [Orange becomes first merchant in Fance to offer Wero for bill payments](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48337/orange-becomes-first-merchant-in-fance-to-offer-wero-for-bill-payments?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

**Twenty-one global banks commit to joint stablecoin venture with euro token as priority**

*Eight European lenders – including Deutsche Bank, Lloyds and Credit Agricole – are among the institutions planning a dollar-backed stablecoin for 2027, with a euro-denominated token next in line and MiCA compliance built in from the start.*

A consortium of 21 financial institutions announced on September 1 that they will establish a new company in the second half of 2026 to issue stablecoins for payments and digital asset settlement. The venture will begin with a US dollar-denominated token, targeting a market launch in the first half of 2027, and has identified a euro stablecoin as its immediate expansion priority. The group said the product is intended to comply with the GENIUS Act in the US and the Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation in the EU.

The European contingent is substantial: Banco Santander, BBVA, Commerzbank, Credit Agricole, Deutsche Bank, Lloyds Banking Group, Rabobank and UBS have all committed. North American members include Bank of America, Citi, Goldman Sachs, Wells Fargo and Fidelity Investments, with MUFG Bank, Standard Bank and others rounding out the roster across Asia, the Middle East and Africa. JPMorgan is absent – the bank has said it will deepen its existing JPM Coin and Kinexys deposit token infrastructure rather than join the consortium.

The venture enters a market dominated by Tether and Circle, but its competitive logic rests on the participating banks' existing customer relationships, compliance infrastructure and payment network access. A separate group of 37 institutions has formed Qivalis to launch a euro-denominated stablecoin later this year, with BBVA participating in both initiatives. The ECB has warned that privately issued stablecoins could pose risks to monetary policy and financial stability – concerns that will sharpen as bank-backed tokens move closer to everyday payments.

*Sources: [Group of leading international financial institutions to establish stablecoin enterprise](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/group-of-leading-international-financial-institutions-to-establish-stablecoin-enterprise-302866318.html) — PR Newswire*

**Allica Bank applies for Swedish licence as first step into European SME lending**

*A Swedish banking licence would give the UK challenger a passport to serve small businesses across the European Economic Area, adding to a growing list of UK fintechs seeking EU footholds.*

Allica Bank has applied to Finansinspektionen, Sweden's financial regulator, for a banking licence that would mark its first expansion outside the UK. The bank has established a Swedish legal entity and appointed a local leadership team headed by Rickard Westlund, with Javier Ubillos as chief technology officer, Victor Ramstrom as chief product and operating officer and Samuel Tawadros as chief financial officer.

Allica focuses on businesses with between five and 250 employees – a segment it says generates around a third of UK GDP but remains underserved by incumbents. CEO Richard Davies said Sweden was chosen for its digital economy, concentrated banking market and the opportunity to serve similar businesses. The bank has lent more than £4 billion to UK businesses since securing its UK licence in 2019 and reported £37 million in statutory pre-tax profit last year. The move follows a $155 million Series D round in February that valued Allica at close to $1.2 billion.

A Swedish licence would also allow Allica to passport services into other EU markets over time. Davies has said the Netherlands and Ireland are among the next targets. Lucy Rigby, economic secretary to the Treasury, welcomed the expansion as evidence of the UK's position as a base for financial services firms. Allica joins a pattern of UK-authorised fintechs seeking EU banking access – Zilch acquired Finland's Fjord Bank earlier in 2026 to achieve a similar outcome.

*Sources: [Allica Bank applies for banking licence in Sweden](https://www.retailbankerinternational.com/news/allica-bank-sweden-banking-licence/) — Retail Banker International*

**Mollie completes €1.1bn GoCardless acquisition, creating pan-European payments group**

*The deal unites card acquiring and bank payment infrastructure under a single platform serving 350,000 businesses, marking a further round of consolidation in European mid-market payments.*

Mollie, the Amsterdam-based payments provider, completed its acquisition of GoCardless on September 1. The deal, first announced in December 2025 and valued at €1.1 billion, was structured with more than 90% of the consideration paid in shares. The combined group now serves over 350,000 businesses across more than 30 markets, with a combined valuation of roughly €3 billion. Mollie chief executive Koen Koppen leads the enlarged group, while GoCardless co-founder Hiroki Takeuchi continues to run GoCardless as a separately branded unit – operating as "GoCardless, a Mollie company".

The acquisition brings together Mollie's card and local payment method capabilities with GoCardless's bank payment infrastructure, which covers direct debit and open banking pay-by-bank services in 38 countries. The €1.1 billion price tag represents roughly half of GoCardless's $2.1 billion peak valuation from 2022 – a measure of how far fintech valuations have corrected since the pandemic-era highs. GoCardless had recently reached its first profitable quarter following a period of cost-cutting that included reducing its workforce by roughly a fifth.

The deal fits a pattern across European payments: mid-market providers combining card acquiring, account-to-account payments and adjacent financial services to compete with larger integrated platforms such as Adyen and Stripe. For GoCardless's open banking and direct debit merchants, the integration into Mollie's broader platform could accelerate cross-sell into card acceptance and business financing. How quickly the two platforms are technically integrated will determine whether the combined group can deliver on that promise.

*Sources: [Mollie completes GoCardless acquisition](https://thepaypers.com/mergers-aquisitions-and-investments/news/mollie-finalises-gocardless-acquisition-to-expand-payments-offer) — The Paypers*
